english_paragraphs: Greyback cane beetles, whose larvae devour roots, were plaguing lucrative sugar plantations in Queensland, north-eastern Australia. In June 1935 Queensland imported 102 cane toads, bulky amphibians native to the Americas, from Hawaii. That August about 2,400 of their young were released. Biological control, setting one species against a pest, had an ambitious new recruit.

The hasty plan met opposition. In November 1935 an insect expert, Walter Froggatt, persuaded officials to halt releases; after Queensland's lobbying, they resumed in September 1936. The scheme flopped: the toads barely dented beetle numbers, perhaps because the insects stayed high up on cane stalks.

The toads thrived instead. With few foes and fertile females spawning thousands of eggs, they multiplied unchecked. Their invasion frontier, creeping about ten kilometres a year at first, accelerated to about 50 a year in the tropical north. In February 2009 the first known toad breached Western Australia's border.

Toxin glands in their skin make them a deadly meal. Numbers of goannas (large lizards) and northern quolls (small marsupial hunters) have slumped in places; some local quoll populations were wiped out. The toads have wreaked havoc, but the damage is uneven; some species have prospered.

Biological control can triumph. From 1926 the cactus moth, Cactoblastis, cleared most prickly pear, an invasive cactus, from Queensland and New South Wales within about a decade. Tested first, its larvae starved rather than eat fifteen other plants; the toads faced no such test. Under an October 1984 law, recruits now face stringent scrutiny. The blunder was born of haste and sealed by lobbying that overrode a warning: an untested ally, once loose, may never be recalled.

这个**草率的**(hasty)计划遭到了**反对**(opposition)。1935年11月，昆虫专家沃尔特·弗罗格特**说服**(persuaded)官员**停止**(halt)释放；经昆士兰州**游说**(lobbying)，释放于1936年9月**恢复**(resumed)。这套**计划/方案**(scheme)**彻底失败**(flopped)：蟾蜍几乎没能**削减**(dented)甲虫的数量，或许是因为这些昆虫一直待在甘蔗**茎秆**(stalks)的高处。

蟾蜍自己反倒**兴旺**(thrived)起来。**天敌**(foes)寥寥，**能生育的**(fertile)雌蟾**产下**(spawning)数千枚卵，它们**不受遏制地**(unchecked)**大量繁殖**(multiplied)。它们的**入侵**(invasion)**前沿**(frontier)起初每年缓慢行进约十公里，到了**热带**(tropical)北部，**加快**(accelerated)到每年约50公里。2009年2月，已知的第一只蟾蜍**突破了**(breached)西澳大利亚州的边界。

它们皮肤里的**毒素**(Toxin)**腺体**(glands)，使它们成为了一顿致命的餐食。巨蜥（大型**蜥蜴**(lizards)）和北袋鼬（一种小型**有袋类**(marsupial)猎手）的数量在一些地方**锐减**(slumped)；部分地方的袋鼬种群被**彻底消灭**(wiped out)。蟾蜍**造成了**(wreaked havoc)**严重破坏**(wreaked havoc)，但损害并**不均衡**(uneven)；有些物种反而**繁荣了**(prospered)起来。

生物防治也能**大获成功**(triumph)。从1926年起，仙人掌螟这种**蛾子**(moth)在约十年内清除了大部分“**带刺的**(prickly)梨”，这是一种**外来入侵的**(invasive)**仙人掌**(cactus)，清除范围遍及昆士兰州和新南威尔士州。这种蛾子放出前经过检验，其**幼虫**(larvae)宁可**饿死**(starved)也不吃另外十五种植物；蟾蜍却从未受过这样的检验。根据1984年10月通过的一部法律，如今新兵都要经过**严格的**(stringent)**认真彻底的审查**(scrutiny)。这个**大错**(blunder)起于**仓促**(haste)，又因**游说**(lobbying)**压过了**(overrode)警告而成定局：**未经检验的**(untested)**盟友**(ally)一旦**放出**(loose)，就可能再也**召不回来**(recalled)。

sentences.chinese_source: 它们皮肤里的**毒素**(Toxin)**腺体**(glands)，使它们成为了一顿致命的餐食。

sentences.english: Numbers of goannas (large lizards) and northern quolls (small marsupial hunters) have slumped in places; some local quoll populations were wiped out.
sentences.chinese_source: 巨蜥（大型**蜥蜴**(lizards)）和北袋鼬（一种小型**有袋类**(marsupial)猎手）的数量在一些地方**锐减**(slumped)；部分地方的袋鼬种群被**彻底消灭**(wiped out)。

sentences.english: The toads have wreaked havoc, but the damage is uneven; some species have prospered.
sentences.chinese_source: 蟾蜍**造成了**(wreaked havoc)**严重破坏**(wreaked havoc)，但损害并**不均衡**(uneven)；有些物种反而**繁荣了**(prospered)起来。
生物防治也能**大获成功**(triumph)。

sentences.english: From 1926 the cactus moth, Cactoblastis, cleared most prickly pear, an invasive cactus, from Queensland and New South Wales within about a decade.
sentences.chinese_source: 从1926年起，仙人掌螟这种**蛾子**(moth)在约十年内清除了大部分“**带刺的**(prickly)梨”，这是一种**外来入侵的**(invasive)**仙人掌**(cactus)，清除范围遍及昆士兰州和新南威尔士州。

sentences.english: Tested first, its larvae starved rather than eat fifteen other plants; the toads faced no such test.
sentences.chinese_source: 这种蛾子放出前经过检验，其**幼虫**(larvae)宁可**饿死**(starved)也不吃另外十五种植物；蟾蜍却从未受过这样的检验。

sentences.english: Under an October 1984 law, recruits now face stringent scrutiny.
sentences.chinese_source: 根据1984年10月通过的一部法律，如今新兵都要经过**严格的**(stringent)**认真彻底的审查**(scrutiny)。

sentences.english: The blunder was born of haste and sealed by lobbying that overrode a warning: an untested ally, once loose, may never be recalled.
sentences.chinese_source: 这个**大错**(blunder)起于**仓促**(haste)，又因**游说**(lobbying)**压过了**(overrode)警告而成定局：**未经检验的**(untested)**盟友**(ally)一旦**放出**(loose)，就可能再也**召不回来**(recalled)。

approved_summary: 1935年，澳大利亚昆士兰引进102只甘蔗蟾蜍，放出约2,400只后代，想控制啃食甘蔗根系的甲虫。
昆虫专家曾促成暂停释放，地方游说却使1936年恢复；蟾蜍释放前缺少食性检验，警告最终被压过。
甲虫几乎没减少，或因它们待在高处；蟾蜍却天敌少、产卵多，在热带北部每年扩散约50公里。
蟾蜍的皮肤毒素使巨蜥、北袋鼬在部分地区锐减，某些袋鼬种群消失；也有物种反而兴盛。
仙人掌螟经检验不吃另15种植物，后来成功控制入侵仙人掌；1984年立法要求严格审查生物防治引种。
